meta.title: BUILT
meta.author: Joe Guadagnino / Lupton Associates
meta.style: Apple product-film grammar on live footage: black is a material, type sits alone on it with enormous margins, headlines build rather than slam, product beats and black type cards alternate, and one colour (the sage) carries the whole film. Every shot moves now — a real camera move on every frame.
meta.note: Fourth pass, and the one that answers 'cinematic'. Joe's five product stills each went into Higgsfield seedance 2.5 (mode omni_reference) as the start_image of an image-to-video generation, so the frame he approved is literally frame one of the clip and the model only supplies the camera move and the physics. Nothing is invented footage. The three macros were pre-cropped to 16:9 and upscaled to 1920x1080; the two hero shots stayed 4:5 native. Earlier passes failed for the opposite reasons: pass 1 and 2 were social-video grammar (bottom-pinned captions over wall-to-wall imagery, a blurred fill behind the 16:9 product shots), pass 3 fixed the grammar but left every frame a static photograph.
meta.footage: Joe Guadagnino product photography (supplied 2026-09-11), animated with Higgsfield seedance 2.5 image-to-video, 5 s each at 32.5 credits. public/img/bu_*.png are the source stills; public/vid/bu_*.mp4 are the clips. bu_fracture.png is the exact frame the heroA orbit stops on, so the cut into the fracture is invisible.

grid: 120 BPM under everything. Shot changes land on Joe's spoken words (2.9, 4.4, 7.4, 10.4 s); the structural beats — fracture, slam, hero, end card — sit on the music grid at 13, 19.85, 23, 27.5 s.

shots.visual: black card; 'Every part you buy / starts as a print.' types itself on with a sage caret
shots.vo: Every part you buy starts as a print.

shots.visual: Joe's laser macro. The camera rushes in low along the plate to the cutting head; sparks streak past the lens. One word, lower third.
Joe's press-brake macro. Slow heavy push-in with a lateral drift; the plate hinges shut about the bend line, a specular highlight travelling the closing line. Slowed to 0.9x.
Joe's MIG arc. The camera arcs right to left around the torch, low over the table; the arc strobes and the torch advances along the bead.
The object alone on pure black, turning in a slow orbit under a raking key. 82% frame height in 16:9, native in 4:5. 'Finished.' in sage below it. Slowed to 0.9x.
The frame the orbit stops on, fractured into four slabs drifting apart on black, draining of colour
shots.vo: Most buyers run that across four different shops. Four purchase orders, four people to call when the holes don't line up.

shots.visual: the slabs snap shut in 10 frames on the score's hit; white flash; 'Under one roof.' in the black beneath
shots.vo: We do it under one roof.

shots.visual: Second angle, alone on black, a slow push-in craning down as the part grows in frame; the three 'one' lines build below it. Slowed to 0.92x.
shots.vo: One print, one project manager, one team that owns the fit.

shots.vo: Send us the print. Let's build it together. Luptons dot com.

voiceover.status: FINAL — Joe Guadagnino's own recording (Webster_Golf_Club_7.m4a, 34.8 s, one continuous take).
voiceover.processing: highpass 85 Hz to drop room rumble, afftdn nr=10 for broadband hiss, alimiter; sliced only at Joe's own pauses (silencedetect -45 dB / 0.22 s), each phrase RMS-matched to -20 dB with 12 ms fades.
voiceover.tempo: BU6, BU7 and BU8 run atempo=1.06 — Joe's read of the problem section is more deliberate than the placeholder, and the 6% lift lets it hand off to the slam line on the beat. Everything else is at his natural pace.
wordingChanges: Joe said 'four DIFFERENT shops' (script said 'four shops') — on-screen label stays the condensed 'Four shops.'
Joe said 'one TEAM that owns the fit' (script said 'one shop') — the on-screen line was changed to 'One team that owns the fit.' so the caption matches the voice.
voiceover.verified: audio-only transcription over black confirmed all phrases and their wording before slicing; assembled master re-verified the same way.
voiceover.note: BU8 joins two of Joe's breaths ('four people to call' / 'when the holes don't line up') with the gap tightened from 0.70 s to 0.18 s.

music.bed: bu_music.wav — original numpy score, 120 BPM. Sub pulse every beat, 16th hats opening up as the film builds, A-minor-pentatonic arpeggio entering at 4 s and lifting an octave at the hero, riser 17.5-19.5 s, big low hit + crack + shimmer on the slam at 19.5 s, resolve at 27.5 s, fade 31.2-33.0 s.
music.license: original — no third-party music, no credit required in the post

sfx: the stills carry no ambience, so only the hits: subbass on the open and on 'Finished.', snap on the brake cut, strike on the weld cut, shatter as the fracture begins, strike on the slam impact, resolve under the end card

typeSystem.scale: measured against frame height, so type occupies the same share of screen in both cuts
typeSystem.reveal: fade + 16px rise + 1.035 scale over 11 frames, ease-out — it arrives, it does not attack
typeSystem.position: dead centre on black cards; lower third when it shares the frame with the object

cutting.note: Clips are 24 fps sources in a 30 fps composition; Remotion maps by time, so the rate is the only speed control.

framing.16:9: macros full-bleed with a bottom scrim; hero clips as plates at 82% frame height on pure black, wide flanks and all.
framing.4:5: macros stay 16:9, held as a scope band 1.45x frame width high on black so the single word lives in real black underneath; hero clips are native 4:5 and fill.
framing.why: Cropping a 16:9 macro into 4:5 would have thrown away two thirds of the width. A letterboxed band on black is the honest move and reads as deliberate.
